blockers.title: The Ed25519 verifier has a key digest but no closed acquisition and same-object join for the public-key bytes
evidence: v41 correctly defines an Ed25519 algorithm, 64-byte signature, domain-separated message, and a four-field builderRoot whose identityEvidence.digest is SHA-256 of a raw 32-byte key. The signed Linux form nevertheless carries only builderRoot, builderRootDigest, and builderSignature. A four-field DIGEST-BOUND signedEntry contains an identity digest and origin policy, not the digest preimage bytes.
signature defines the verification key as 'the 32-byte key whose digest is builderRootDigest'. SHA-256 is not invertible; knowing the digest does not produce the key bytes required by Ed25519 verify.

No builderPublicKey field or builderRootObservation is defined. No operation invokes originSearchPolicy for this root, requires the resolved object to be exactly 32 bytes, hashes those acquired bytes, binds them by a same-resolution association token to builderRoot, and passes those identical bytes to verify.

The generic retained event schema records resolvedObjectIdentity, not raw resolved bytes. The PATHLESS OS-ABI later event omits resolvedObjectIdentity and retains only builderSignature and builderRootDigest. A separate builder-root resolution event is neither required nor joined to builderAttestation.

Concrete reproducibility test: give two validators the complete signed Linux object, measured member/P, and retained PATHLESS event. Both have the key digest and signature, but neither has the 32 key bytes from any named input. One can reject as unavailable; another can fetch a key through an unstated path. The contract supplies no common operation or association record that selects the latter behavior.

This is the same data-type boundary the contract handles explicitly for TPM quotes by retaining akTpmtPublic before signature verification. A public-key digest authenticates candidate bytes after acquisition; it is not itself a public key.
blockers.impact: The sole structural kexec-absent proof is not executable from the closed signed and retained inputs. Literal implementations reject every Linux entry, while implementations that invent an external key-acquisition path no longer share one auditable trust-root observation.
blockers.requiredRepair: Carry the exact 32-byte raw key in a pinned encoding, or define a builderRoot resolution observation that obtains exactly 32 bytes through the signed root's originSearchPolicy. Require SHA-256 of those acquired bytes to equal builderRoot.identityEvidence.digest, signedObject.builderRootDigest, and later.builderRootDigest; bind acquisition to the qualification run with the same-event association discipline; and require Ed25519 verify to consume those identical bytes. Add absent-key, non-32-byte object, wrong-object, path-retarget, cross-event composition, and correct-key vectors.

shouldFix.title: The governing IKCONFIG branch no longer defines unmatched, reversed, or extra-marker disposition
evidence: v41 correctly makes the new branch object GOVERNING, removes the old unconditional ikconfigPair step, and limits extract/serialization/signedCarriage to presentBranch.

presentBranch now triggers when P contains any IKCFG_ST/IKCFG_ED pair and requires exactly one pair; absentBranch triggers on zero pairs. Neither clause defines whether a lone start marker, lone end marker, reversed markers, one valid pair plus a stray marker, or nested/overlapping occurrences counts as absent, malformed, or multiple.

The v40-era exact grammar refused reversed, nested, and overlapping markers, but v41's governing sentence supersedes earlier marker text. Implementations cannot consistently import the old disposition while also treating the new object as governing.

Concrete divergence: P containing IKCFG_ED before IKCFG_ST has zero forward pairs under one parser and takes absentBranch, while another parser detects malformed/reversed markers and refuses. P with one valid pair plus a trailing IKCFG_ED similarly can be counted as one pair or malformed/multiple.
shouldFix.impact: Identical P bytes can qualify on the absent branch, refuse, or enter the present branch depending on pairing strategy. The corroborating configuration result and optional digest shape are not deterministic.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Define marker-token cardinality and ordered pairing over every occurrence, including lone, reversed, nested, overlapping, and stray markers. State the exact absent condition as no marker tokens or no valid pair, whichever is intended, and add vectors for every malformed class.

shouldFix.title: Signed headerKind is not explicitly equated to the architecture-dispatch branch that produced P
evidence: preimage restricts headerKind to x86-setup-0x1f1, arm64-zimg-loaded, or arm64-image-0x38, but architectureDispatch does not output an actualHeaderKind value and no fieldwise equality joins the chosen branch to preimage.headerKind.

consumePredicate compares payloadDigest and the fixed consumeRelation token but only says the builder signs 'with headerKind'. It does not state that x86 dispatch MUST use x86-setup-0x1f1, arm64 zboot MUST use arm64-zimg-loaded, and arm64 uncompressed MUST use arm64-image-0x38.

Concrete counterexample: a valid x86 member and P are signed with preimage.headerKind arm64-image-0x38. Machine, member hashes, payloadDigest, consumeRelation, kernelRelease, and Ed25519 all pass under the literal clauses; only an inferred, unstated branch equality would refuse.
shouldFix.impact: The signed consume predicate is not fieldwise joined to the parser decision it claims to attest, so validators can disagree on a mismatched but enumerated token.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Make architectureDispatch return actualHeaderKind and require preimage.headerKind to equal it. Add the three correct mappings and every cross-kind mismatch to G22 vectors and NT-TCB-KEXEC.
